2. The plaintiffs filed the suit for a declaration of their right of easement and for a permanent injunction. The suit was instituted on 25-8-66. Upon the application for temporary injunction, filed on behalf of the plaintiffs, the learned Munsif recorded the following order on 10-9-66: 

 "Plaintiffs filed a petition under Order 39 rule 1 C.P.C. by swearing an affidavit praying fog restraining the defendants from encroaching the disputed land on the ground stated therein. Heard, Issue notice upon the defendants to show cause within 7 days of receipt of notice as to why temporary injunction as prayed for should not be granted against them. Plaintiffs to put the requisite-copies of petition at once. 

 "Plaintiffs file certain documents as per list. Let this be accepted. Plaintiff’s petition dated 10-9-66 for issuing of temporary injunction against the defendants is put up today. Perused document and found a prima facie case in favour of the plaintiffs. Issue temporary injunction as prayed for against the defendants. Plaintiffs to file requisite etc." 

 On 7-1-67 the learned Munsif recorded an Order: "Summons upon defendants duly served." Before the order dated 22-11-66 granting injunction was passed, the record does not indicate that the notice directed to be issued in terms the order dated 10-9-66 was served on the, defendants. Meanwhile; on the plaintiffs application complaining violation of the order of injunction, Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1968 was started against the defendants on 25-1-68. The defendants thereafter filed an application under Order 39 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 30-3-68. This application came up for hearing on 23-7-68 and was rejected for default of the defendants. An appeal was taken against the said order dated 23-7-68 and the learned District Judge dismissed the same. 

 6. Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury the Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs opposite party contends that the application under Order 39 rule 4 C.P.C. was not maintainable. Mr. Chowdhury submits that the application under Order 39 rule 4 was made long after the defendants entered appearance in the suit. This application was filed after miscellaneous case No. 9 of 1966 was started to frustrate the consequences of violation of the order of injunction. 

 7. The aforesaid observations, in the facts and circumstances of the instant case, are clearly against the plaintiffs inasmuch as the order of injunction dated 22-11-66 was passed in the absence of the defendants, no-notice to show cause being served on them. The defendants had no opportunity of being heard before the order of injunction was made. Mr. Chowdhury failed to point out that the defendants by their own fault neglected to advance their case at the hearing on 22-11-66 and as such they were precluded to put up their case under Rule 4 of Order 39. Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury next relied upon the case of Mohammad Khalilur Rahman Vs. Parasanath and others AIR 1964 Patna 165. This case is also against Mr. Chowdhury.
